newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN SAYS SOUTH AFRICA WILL BEAT LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TEICHMANN SAYS SOUTH AFRICA WILL BEAT LIONS.

text.p: Springbok captain Gary Teichmann, while concerned that his side's preparations have been severely disrupted this week with the loss of three key backline players, says he is confident South Africa can level the test series agaist the British Lions on Saturday.
In the last two days injury has deprived South African of experienced right wing James Small and centres Japie Mulder and Edrich Lubbe.

Western Province wing Pieter Rossouw and Northern Transvaal centre Danie van Schalkwyk were drafted into the squad as late replacements on Tuesday. The Lions won the first test in Cape Town last Saturday 25-16.

"Obviously these late withdrawals don't help us in preparing for what is really a crucial match. We are fully aware that we made a lot of mistakes in Cape Town and the Lions were quick to take advantage," Teichmann said in an interview.
"But I firmly believe we can bounce back and square the series here in Durban. We just have to keep calm and not let the pressure get to us as we did last year against the All Blacks.
"And we can't afford to be too negative about our Newlands defeat. There were some positives for us in that game and we must build on those."
Teichmann said his side had never underestimated the strength of the 1997 Lions -- "although I think a lot of the South African media did".

"But the only way you can prove them (our critics) wrong is on the field. Yesterday at Kings Park our practice was sharp. There were no mistakes and I think that shows that the pressure isn't getting to the guys."
South Africa were announcing their side for the second test against the Lions at 1230 GMT.
